hints: A 2D Fenwick tree supports changing one cell and summing a rectangle.
Store counts at Fenwick ancestors in both row and column dimensions.
A rectangle sum uses four prefix sums by inclusion-exclusion.
analogy: The 2D tree updates a cell's row and column ancestor buckets, while queries combine four corners.
example: Toggling one tree from empty to occupied changes a rectangle containing it by one.
algorithm: Build a 2D Fenwick tree. A toggle changes the cell by +1 or -1; query rectangle [y1,x1]..[y2,x2] from four 2D prefix queries.
correctness: The 2D Fenwick prefix returns exactly the sum of its top-left rectangle; inclusion-exclusion isolates the requested rectangle and point updates maintain all containing buckets.
complexity: O(log n log m) per update/query and O(nm) storage.
